accuracy.reason: Lifetime, freshness, and presence are distinguished accurately without treating TTL as a refresh timer.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

mechanisms.reason: Expiration and capacity removal lead to a later application fetch through the established miss path.

evidence.quote: Sets how long an entry may remain before it expires. A 60-second TTL does not refresh the product every minute; a later miss must load it again.

coherence.reason: Uses the existing product entry and cache-aside flow to explain two removal causes.

evidence.quote: A product can be evicted before its TTL ends. Some configurations reject new entries when full instead of evicting existing ones.

decisions.reason: Sufficient limits and alternative full-cache behavior for the target; expiry-policy tuning is appropriately outside this target.

outcomes.reason: All timing cases are correct: 09:02 stale hit, 09:06 expired miss, and 09:04 evicted miss. Answer distinguishes capacity from time removal, denies refresh and freshness guarantees, and attributes subsequent load to the API. Quotes entail each claim with the existing miss flow.
